P1_orbit_quotient.interpretation: scipy maps sampled SU(2) unit quaternions to SO(3) rotation matrices; antipodal quaternion pairs collapse to one SO(3) matrix, producing the measured log(2) entropy gap

P2_clifford_bivector.interpretation: Clifford rotor R(theta)=cos(theta/2)+sin(theta/2)e12 over [0,4pi) has 1000 distinct SU(2) elements. Rotor sign canonicalization collapses antipodal pairs to 500 SO(3) classes. Entropy drops by log(2).

P3_sympy_spectral.interpretation: Sympy confirms symbolically: S(SU2) - S(SO3) = log(N) - log(N/2) = log(2) regardless of N. The gap is structural, not a numerical artifact.

P4_su2_so3_double_cover_cross_check.interpretation: Three independent paths (scipy orbit, clifford bivector, sympy spectral) all agree on the log(2) entropy gap for this bounded SU(2)->SO(3) double-cover fixture. This remains classical-baseline evidence and does not promote a higher-stage claim.

N1_z3_unsat_entropy_preservation.interpretation: z3 UNSAT: it is structurally impossible for a 2:1 group homomorphism to preserve orbit entropy. S_G = S_H + delta with delta > 0 (the kernel contributes log(2) entropy), so S_G = S_H is unsatisfiable. The entropy gap is not optional.

B1_z4_z2_cover_gap.interpretation: B1: log(2) gap is not specific to SU(2)->SO(3). Any 2:1 cover produces the same gap. Z4->Z2 (kernel = {0,2}, size 2) gives gap = log(4) - log(2) = log(2). The invariant is: gap = log(|ker(f)|). For 2:1 covers, |ker| = 2, so gap = log(2).

summary.claim: Bounded classical-baseline cross-check: the tested SU(2)->SO(3) double-cover fixtures show a log(2) entropy gap.
